answer: A nebula of small, linked stake pools can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to lock a refundable deposit that only vests after it completes verifiable work witnessed by unrelated peers. A willow-like trust graph grows slowly: new identities start with near-zero weight and gain it only through consistent, attested behaviour over time, while an umber audit trail records every attestation so a sudden burst of new accounts is visible. Creating thousands of sybils then costs thousands of deposits plus weeks of honest-looking work, while honest agents pay only one deposit and time.
